To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CXCR4 and CXCL12 are expressed in lymph nodes and are related to the prognosis of lymph‐ node‐positive lung cancer.

CXCR4/CXR7/CXCL 12 chemokines are associated with prognosis in N1‐N2 lung cancer patients, and CXCR4/CXL12 chemokines play roles in tumor cells in lymph nodes and are associated with poor survival of lung cancer patients with lymph node metastasis.
the CXCR4/CXL12 chemokine expression in primary site and metastatic lymph node is associated with poor overall and progression‐free survival of lymph‐node metastatic NSCLC patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the correlation between CXCR4, CCR7, and CXCL12 and the prognosis of lung cancer patients with lymph node metastasis.
the correlation between CXCR4, CXC7 and CXCL2 chemokine axis expressions and prognosis of lymph‐positive lung cancer.
the CXCR4/CXR7/CXCL 12 chemokine expression in lymph‐node positive NSCLC and its correlation with prognosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CXCL12 in lymph nodes is a prognostic factor for lymph‐node‐involved NSCLC.
high CXCR4 expression of primary site and high CXCL12 expression of metastatic lymph nodes are associated with poor prognosis.
CXCL12 expression by MLN‐tumor cells is an independent prognosticator for OS in lymph‐node positive lung cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CXCR4/CXR7/CXCL 12 chemokine expression is associated with prognosis in lymph‐ node‐ positive non‐small cell lung cancer.

the CXCR4/CXR7/CXCL-12 chemokine system is associated with the prognosis of lymph node positive lung cancer, and the CXCR4 expression at the primary site and the CXCL12 expression at the metastatic lymph nodes were associated with the prognosis, and the combination of these expressions could better predict the prognosis of lung cancer patients.
CXCR4/CXR7/CXCL‐12 chemokine expressions are correlated with lymph node metastasis and prognosis of NSCLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CXCR4/CCL12 axis is associated with the prognosis of lymph‐positive NSCLCs and that CXCL12 in lymph nodes is mainly expressed by tumor cell.
the CXCR4/CCL12 chemokines axis plays important roles not only in the migration of cancer cells to lymph nodes but also in tumor progression of lymph nodes.
expression of CXCR7 in PS and CXCR4/CXR7 in MLN may be a prognostic marker for lymph‐node‐negative NSCLC patients and may predict lymph node metastasis.
